notes: The cascading clauses, the savage deconstruction of corporate language ('nutritional content of a wet napkin'), and the gonzo moral outrage are unmistakably Thompsonesque, but the voice skews more toward his Rolling Stone essay mode than Fear and Loathing — missing the paranoid first-person chaos and drug-addled velocity — while the usability suffers because the rhetorical bravado, however compelling, would likely alarm a legal team and distract consumers from the concrete safety action required.
